description: A via that carried DHT22_DATA between F.Cu and B.Cu is deleted, splitting the net into two islands of copper and leaving a required connection with no copper path between its pads.
seed_target: vias[5] of board_base.json — the DHT22_DATA via at (13.4,16.6), 0.4 mm drill, 0.8 mm diameter. The via was deleted from the vias list. The site was chosen by the rule in mutate.py: among the vias that (1) carry a net whose copper exists on more than one signal layer, so that the via really is a layer transition, and (2) are load-bearing — removing the via opens a required connection that was closed before it was removed — take the one that sorts first on the total order (net, x, y). DHT22_DATA is the only net on this board routed across both layers through a via, and of its two vias only the one at (13.4,16.6) is load-bearing; the other, at (10.2,19.0), is a redundant drop to a through-hole pad that is still reached by the F.Cu track. The result is 7 vias in the base and 6 in the defective board — nothing else changed.
notes: The defect lives in the copper, not in the netlist: the two pads it joined are still on DHT22_DATA, and only the piece of copper that made them one thing is gone. board_base.json passes III.1; board_defective.json fails III.1 (1 of 12 required connections have no copper path) and no other check changes.
